Section 5 • \(P\)3D

5.1 Per-sample (realization-level) 3D power spectrum, \(\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{k}_{\perp},k_\parallel\right)\)

Given one realization \(s\), with the fields \(\delta_i^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda)\) defined on \(\mathcal{A}_\perp\times[\Lambda_a,\Lambda_b]\) as in Sec. 4, we define their finite-domain Fourier transforms \begin{equation} \widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{k}_{\perp},k_\parallel\right) \equiv \frac{1}{(2\pi)^{3/2}} \int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}\! d^2x_\perp \int_{\Lambda_a}^{\Lambda_b}\! d\Lambda\; e^{-i\left(\vec{k}_\perp\cdot\vec{x}_\perp+k_\parallel\Lambda\right)}\, \delta_i^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right), \tag{5.1} \end{equation} and the per-sample 3D cross-power spectrum (periodogram) \begin{equation} \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{k}_{\perp},k_\parallel\right) \equiv \frac{(2\pi)^3}{|\mathcal{A}_\perp|\,L_\Lambda}\; \widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{k}_{\perp},k_\parallel\right)\, \widetilde{\delta}_j^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{k}_{\perp},k_\parallel\right)^{*}. \tag{5.2} \end{equation} The normalization by the volume \(|\mathcal{A}_\perp|\,L_\Lambda\) makes \(\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\) independent of the size of the domain, with units \([x_\perp]^2\,[\Lambda]\).

For real-valued fields, \(\widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s)}(-\vec{k}_\perp,-k_\parallel)=\widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s)}(\vec{k}_\perp,k_\parallel)^*\), and therefore \begin{equation} \widehat{P}_{ji}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{k}_{\perp},k_\parallel\right) = \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{k}_{\perp},k_\parallel\right)^{*} = \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(-\vec{k}_{\perp},-k_\parallel\right), \tag{5.3} \end{equation} the Fourier counterpart of Eq. (4.3): exchanging \(i\leftrightarrow j\) is a complex conjugation, and it is an exact identity for every realization when both components of \(\vec{k}\) are flipped at once. In particular, \(\widehat{P}_{ii}^{(s)}\) is real and even under \(\vec{k}\to-\vec{k}\), and \(\widehat{P}_{ij,\mathrm{sym}}^{(s)}\equiv\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}+\widehat{P}_{ji}^{(s)}=2\,\mathrm{Re}\,\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}\). Flipping the components separately:

  • Transverse flip, \(\vec{k}_\perp\to-\vec{k}_\perp\) at fixed \(k_\parallel\): not an identity of the periodogram; it holds for the ensemble under isotropy around the line of sight, \(P_{ij}(-\vec{k}_\perp,k_\parallel)=P_{ij}(\vec{k}_\perp,k_\parallel)\). Combined with Eq. (5.3), it gives \(P_{ij}(\vec{k}_\perp,-k_\parallel)=P_{ij}(\vec{k}_\perp,k_\parallel)^*=P_{ji}(\vec{k}_\perp,k_\parallel)\).

  • Line-of-sight flip, \(k_\parallel\to-k_\parallel\) at fixed \(\vec{k}_\perp\): by the previous item, it is a complex conjugation. The asymmetry of a cross-correlation under \(\Delta\to-\Delta\) is therefore carried by the imaginary part of \(P_{ij}\), which is odd in \(k_\parallel\) (e.g. a relative offset \(\Delta_0\) between two lines, \(\xi_{ij}(\vec{r}_\perp,\Delta)\propto\xi(\vec{r}_\perp,\Delta-\Delta_0)\), becomes a phase \(P_{ij}\propto e^{+ik_\parallel\Delta_0}P\)). For autocorrelations \(P_{ii}\) is real and even in \(k_\parallel\).
